1.explanation: BaseVector.js is where the layer’s declutter flag is stored and where renderDeclutter is invoked when declutter is enabled. When opacity changes, the declutter tree is still built in BaseVectorLayer but subsequent rendering fails to mix in the new opacity. CanvasVectorLayerRenderer.js is responsible for actually drawing both normal and decluttered items; its renderFrame and renderDeclutter implementations do not apply the layer’s globalAlpha/composition context correctly to decluttered symbols. As a result, once you call setOpacity on a decluttered layer, the renderer clears the buffers and skips drawing anything (or draws it fully transparent), making the layer disappear.
1.bug_scenario: On the OpenLayers vector‐labels example, when you enable decluttering on a VectorLayer and then call setOpacity (e.g. to 0.5) after a delay, the entire vector layer vanishes instead of simply becoming semi-transparent. In the screenshot sequence you see the points and text labels drawn initially, and then the map goes blank once setOpacity(0.5) is applied.
